subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Salience of Tax Burden
description: A 60-second lesson on Salience of Tax Burden.

hook.text: A store posts prices without sales tax. You see $10 and pay $10.80. Chetty showed that making tax visible at the shelf.

buildup.text: Tax salience determines how much taxes influence behavior. If taxes are hidden or separated from prices, people.

discovery.text: Finkelstein found that when tolls switched from cash to electronic, drivers barely noticed increases.

twist.text: Governments benefit from low salience. Income tax withheld from paychecks feels smaller than writing a single annual.

climax.text: Tax transparency isn't about honesty. When citizens feel taxes, they scrutinize government spending more.

punchline.text: Taxes you do not see are taxes you do not question.

quiz.question: What did Chetty's study show about tax-inclusive pricing?
options: Making tax visible at the shelf had no effect on purchases
Making tax visible reduced purchases by 8%
Consumers preferred stores with hidden taxes

details.summary: Tax salience affects behavior: taxes included in posted prices reduce demand more than equivalent taxes added at checkout. When the tax burden is less visible, people spend more because they underestimate or ignore the true cost of their purchases.
details.whyItMatters: How taxes are displayed changes economic behavior independent of the tax rate itself. Less salient taxes generate less consumer resistance, which is why governments and retailers have incentives to obscure tax costs in different ways.
takeaways: Taxes included in displayed prices reduce demand more than add-on taxes
Consumers systematically underweight taxes they cannot easily see
Tax salience design is a policy choice with real economic consequences

faq.question: How much does tax visibility affect consumer spending?
faq.answer: Studies show that making sales tax fully visible in shelf prices reduces demand by 5 to 8 percent compared to the same tax added at checkout. Consumers react to the sticker price and underweight costs they face later.

faq.question: Should governments make all taxes more salient?
faq.answer: It depends on the goal. More salient taxes increase accountability and informed choice but reduce consumption and generate political resistance. Less salient taxes are easier to implement but may hide the true cost of government from citizens.
